newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eiffage sees return to profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Eiffage sees return to profit in 1997.

text.p: Public works group Eiffage said it expected to return to profit next year by reducing its break-even point -- unless turnover falls more than eight percent from 1996 levels and assuming its margins are sustained.
The company said in a statement that a return to profitability was assured "as long as turnover is not more than eight percent below 1996 levels and our margins...do not deteriorate further".
Its outlook for the industry was bleak. The company said competition was running high and a rebound in French road and building works was not expected over the next 18 months.

Eiffage said it aimed to reduce fixed costs by 13 percent annually over the next two years, while a programme to sell around one billion francs of non-core assets would help its balance sheet by generating capital gains.

The company earlier reported a first-half net attributable loss of 890 million francs for the first half of 1996. It said it expected to lose around 900 million francs for the full year and it suspended its 1996 dividend payment.
Its stock was trading at 359.10 francs, down 40.90 francs, at 1020 GMT after a partial recovery from a slide to a session low of 326 francs.
